text:
Simone: FYI canary deploy for tf-gpupools v3.2.0 is stuck in ArgoCD sync, plan shows provider/aws v5.11 -> v5.15 and KMS alias replacement. Anyone else seeing this?
ops-bot: CI pipeline failed: terraform-plan (canary/gpupool) — exit 1. Link: https://ci.internal/runs/4567 :warning:
Rajan: pinged the canary, looking. initial thought: lockfile mismatch between repo and pipeline worker. Did we update the .terraform.lock.hcl?
Simone: we bumped the module in main and created a canary branch, but I didn't touch lockfile, module change pulled in provider alias usage in module/gpupool/kms.tf
Marta: if the module adds a provider alias with kms_key_id computed via data source, TF will treat alias changes as provider reconfiguration. Might require `terraform state replace-provider` in the canary preparer job.
Liam: can we avoid state surgery by pinning provider version in module and regenerating lockfile in the canary image? CI images are using TF 1.5.7. The lockfile in repo is old.
Rajan: adding more detail — plan output: ```diff
- resource "aws_kms_alias" "gpukey_alias" {
-   name = "alias/rw-gpu-01"
- }
+ resource "aws_kms_alias" "gpukey_alias" {
+   name = "alias/rw-gpu-01-<region>"
+ }
``` This suggests a change in how the module computes alias suffix for regional variants.
Simone: this is risky for live Dedicated fleets, since kms alias rename would break instance startup. Want to gate it.
Megan: proposal: add a GitOps canary gate script that runs `terraform plan -out=canary.plan` then `terraform show -json canary.plan` and runs a policy check for kms_aws_alias and provider.reinstall signals. If any detected, fail fast. I can mock a policy in rego and add to repo.
Rajan: short-term mitigation: revert module bump in canary branch, then create a patch that only includes provider version pin + lockfile update, run the canary, then apply the alias rename in a follow-up with an explicit migration plan.
Marta: also watch ArgoCD: it was auto-pruning the old module tag cause of image-tag sync. We should disable auto-sync for infra modules until migration is complete.
Simone: agreed. I'll open a PR to pin provider in the module and include the regenerated .terraform.lock.hcl. Who can trigger the fresh plan on CI image? @Liam?
Liam: will do. Running in debug container to reproduce locally first. cmds I'm using: ```bash
TF_CLI_CONFIG_FILE=$(pwd)/ci-tfrc terraform init -upgrade -lockfile=auto
terraform plan -var-file=env/canary.tfvars -out=canary.plan
```
ops-bot: manual intervention required. Marking canary as blocked until 1982345800.
Simone: thanks. After we confirm lockfile regen, we should document the rollout steps in infra/runbooks/tf-module-rollouts.md and add a canary gating job in our gitops-pipeline.
Megan: I'll add the rego policy PR and a short CI job to run it. Also suggest we add a `preserve_aliases = true` flag to module to make future renames opt-in.
Rajan: one more note: if we proceed with rename, need a small migration that creates new alias while keeping old alias until instances are migrated (dual-write). Not immediate delete.
Simone: perfect. Let's coordinate on the PRs. tagging this thread for follow-up. :white_check_mark:
